title: Cohomology of the truncation tower
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site], let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on this site, and let $K$ be a cochain complex of sheaves of left $\mathcal R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects; def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For canonical truncations use [def-kun-truncations], and write $R^1\varprojlim$ for the degree-one cohomology of the derived inverse limit of a module tower [det-pe-milnor-sequence]. For each integer $n\geq0$, let
$\tau_{\geq-n}K$ be its canonical truncation, with the quotient maps
$K\to\tau_{\geq-n}K$ and $\tau_{\geq-(n+1)}K\to\tau_{\geq-n}K$. Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$.

1. $H^q(\tau_{\geq-n}K)=0$ for $n<-q$, and for $n\geq-q$ the map
   $H^q(K)\to H^q(\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ is an isomorphism; the transition maps
   $H^q(\tau_{\geq-(n+1)}K)\to H^q(\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ are identities (under these
   isomorphisms) for $n\geq-q$ and maps to $0$ for $n<-q$. In particular they are all
   epimorphisms.
2. $R^1\varprojlim_{n\geq0}H^q(\tau_{\geq-n}K)=0$ and
   $H^q(K)\to\varprojlim_{n\geq0}H^q(\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $a=-n$. By the canonical truncation definition [def-kun-truncations], $\tau_{\geq a}K$ is zero below degree $a$, equals $\operatorname{coker}d^{a-1}$ in degree $a$, and equals $K^i$ above it. Thus its cohomology is zero below $a$. In degree $a$, the kernel of the induced map $K^a/\operatorname{im}d^{a-1}\to K^{a+1}$ is $\ker d^a/\operatorname{im}d^{a-1}$; in degree $a+1$ the image of the incoming differential is still $\operatorname{im}d^a$, and all higher kernel/image quotients are unchanged. These are precisely the cohomology objects of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently $u_n=H^q(K\to\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ is an isomorphism when $n\geq-q$ and its target is zero otherwise.

source.place: Tag 0118, label section-truncations (external cross-reference homology-section-truncations), canonical cochain truncation (fourth item)

proof.text: Write $M_n=H^q(\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ and $t_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$. The quotient maps of complexes satisfy $(K\to\tau_{\geq-(n+1)}K)\mathbin{;} (\tau_{\geq-(n+1)}K\to\tau_{\geq-n}K)=(K\to\tau_{\geq-n}K)$: this is the identity in degrees above $-n$, the quotient in degree $-n$, and the unique map to zero below it. Functoriality gives $t_nu_{n+1}=u_n$. For $n\geq-q$, both $u_n$ and $u_{n+1}$ are isomorphisms, so $u_n^{-1}t_nu_{n+1}=1$; otherwise $M_n=0$. Hence every $t_n$ is epimorphic. Apply [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic] to this tower of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules to obtain $R^1\varprojlim_n M_n=0$.

source.place: Proof, steps 1–2: compatibility of quotient maps and the epimorphic Milnor statement

proof.text: Let $N=\max(0,-q)$. The maps $u_n:H^q(K)\to M_n$ form a cone. For any other cone $(f_n:A\to M_n)_n$, put $f=u_N^{-1}f_N:A\to H^q(K)$. If $n<N$, then $M_n=0$ and $u_nf=f_n$. If $n\geq N$, compatibility with the composite transition $t_{n,N}$ gives $t_{n,N}f_n=f_N$ and $t_{n,N}u_n=u_N$; since $t_{n,N}$ is an isomorphism, $u_nf=f_n$. Uniqueness follows from the component at $N$. Thus this cone is a limit cone, proving that the canonical map $H^q(K)\to\varprojlim_{n\geq0}M_n$ is an isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem truncation_tower_cohomology (X : Scheme.{t}) (R : Sheaf (topology X) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)}) (K : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ) (q : ℤ) : (∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) < -q → IsZero ((milnorCohomologyTower (postnikovTower K) q).obj (op n))) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, -q ≤ (n : ℤ) → IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ))) q)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.πTruncGE (-((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))) q ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (postnikovStep K n) q = HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ))) q) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) < -q → HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (postnikovStep K n) q = 0) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Epi (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (postnikovStep K n) q)) ∧ IsZero (milnorTowerCokernel (milnorCohomologyTower (postnikovTower K) q)) ∧ ∃ f : (HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) q).obj K ⟶ limit (milnorCohomologyTower (postnikovTower K) q), (∀ n : ℕ, f ≫ limit.π (milnorCohomologyTower (postnikovTower K) q) (op n) = HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ))) q) ∧ IsIso f
